object_description: four identical staggered buildings arranged around a central square with introverted courtyards
geometry_property: crown of rooms around a corridor
design_condition: four identical buildings are staggered around a square to initiate a new centrality, taking up the geometry of the planted alley along the sports fields and treating the surroundings as a park

positive: Location and orientation confirm the desire to initiate a new urban centrality around a square
The layout initiates future development by taking up the geometry of the planted alley
The new centrality and rigorous ground plan help bring order to the fragmented urban fabric
A formal relationship with the neighbouring university buildings is established
The four buildings are identical in plan and height, lending unity to the whole
The surrounding area is treated as a park with vegetable gardens
The public programme on the ground floor is laid out around a square serving as a hub for the pathways
The precise siting and well-measured massing provide an appropriate urban and territorial response
Foundations, structure, energy and sustainable development have been well understood and addressed
The compactness of the buildings and the recommended construction methods lead to an economical project
negative: Access to the accommodation is only possible from inside the courtyards via passageways
The disappearance of the corner openings from the first stage makes the courtyards introverted
The courtyards have all become the same and lose identity and relationship with the district
The loss of permeability calls into question their true use value and quality
The similarity of the four buildings suggests no hierarchy of access or differentiated programme distribution
The location of the guest accommodation is undifferentiated
The proximity of facades at the corners places many rooms in an unfortunate face-to-face situation
The position of the children centre and its outdoor spaces in front of busy walkways is unconvincing
The plan and section lack flexibility, making contextual responses difficult and the development potential fixed
The concept of blocks around a central square distant from its neighbours is questionable here
The hierarchical appropriation and use of the courtyards and central square raises questions
The underground hall structures cause problems in relation to the water table and seismic measures
